cases.decision_question: Should finance approve the proposed route as cheaper on recurring cost per accepted result?

required_metric.label: proposed recurring cost per accepted result

cases.situation: Both routes attempt 1,000 jobs. The current route has $800 of provider cost, $200 of shared cost, 900 accepted results, and 4 hours of correction work at $60 per hour. The proposed route has $500 of provider cost, $200 of shared cost, 700 accepted results, and 15 hours of correction work at $60 per hour. All stated costs cover the same period and scope.

claims.text: The proposed route has the lower provider bill.
The proposed route is cheaper after shared cost and required correction work are included.

cases.decision_question: Can finance describe $4,800 as Route B's provider-reported cost from the supplied evidence?
cases.situation: The organization received one $12,000 provider invoice. Usage telemetry attributes 60% of input and output tokens to Route A and 40% to Route B. The invoice also contains shared infrastructure, storage, and batch adjustments that are not assigned to either route. The team multiplies the total invoice by Route B's 40% token share and records $4,800. No provider-reported route-level cost is available.

claims.text: Route B represents 40% of the measured input and output tokens.

cases.decision_question: Should finance approve a claim that the entire workflow became 49.5% cheaper?
cases.situation: A workload processes 1,000,000,000 input tokens in each period. Uncached input costs $2.00 per million tokens and cache reads cost $0.20 per million. Cache reads rise from 10% of input tokens to 60%. Cache-write charges, output, tools, retries, shared infrastructure, and human correction are not supplied. For this bounded comparison, treat the stated cache-read and uncached-input rates as the only input charges.

claims.text: The bounded input charge falls from $1,820 to $920, a reduction of about 49.5%.

cases.decision_question: Should finance approve the proposed route as cheaper at its observed ready-result rate?
cases.situation: The current route costs $10,000 per period and produces 900 ready results from 1,000 attempts. The proposed route costs $8,000 per period and produces 680 ready results from 1,000 attempts. Both totals include provider, shared, and measured human correction cost on the same basis. No one-time change cost applies. Finance wants the proposed route's minimum ready-result rate needed to match the current route's cost per ready result.

claims.text: The proposed route has the lower recurring total.
At a 68% ready-result rate, the proposed route is cheaper per ready result.

cases.decision_question: Should finance approve the migration as cheaper within the remaining four-month contract horizon?
cases.situation: The current route costs $50,000 per month. The proposed route costs $43,000 per month after all recurring provider, shared, and human costs. Migration requires $42,000 of one-time work. Quality, policy, and evidence gates pass, but only four months remain in the current contract horizon and there is no approved value beyond that date.

claims.text: The proposed route lowers recurring cost by $7,000 per month.
The migration is cheaper within the remaining four-month contract horizon.
